title: Edge shadow reconcile for sticky-session metering
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Edge collectors (regionally deployed proxies) emit high-frequency subrequest events and provisional meter records for streaming sessions. Due to sticky-session routing and intermittent edge-level retries, the hosted billing pipeline overcounts tokens and creates noisy late-arrival corrections. This ticket implements a dedicated Delta Ledger Aggregator that runs a shadow reconciliation mode at edge-to-central boundary to produce a single, idempotent billing delta per logical session.
goals: Build a streaming delta aggregator that deduplicates subrequests and collapses provisional meter events into a single canonical ledger entry per session-window
Preserve subsecond latency for read path instrumentation (no added tail latency to user RPCs), run reconciliation asynchronously
Add heuristics for sticky-session routing detection and safe credit gating to avoid double-charging during rollouts
Produce audit-friendly output table for billing that retains provenance (edge-id, route, model, variant, request_id_chain)
Support shadow-mode rollout then gated flip to authoritative ledger once stable
design_notes: Architecture: edge collectors push compact per-subrequest 'meter fragments' to a regional Kafka topic. Delta Ledger Aggregator will subscribe to all regional topics, group events by session_id + customer_id, and maintain a short-lived state (TTL 6 hours) to compact fragments into a canonical delta. We will use Kafka Streams (or Flink) for exactly-once processing; output writes will be idempotent upserts into BigQuery partitioned table (billing.deltas) using composite key (tenant_id, session_window_start, canonical_request_hash). Watermarking: handle late-arrival up to 2 hours, emit provisional reconciliations with a reconciliation_score; finalization step marks deltas as 'settled' after watermark. Idempotency & ordering: include event_seq and causal chain hash to detect replays from edge retries.
tradeoffs:
- Stateful streaming adds infra complexity and cost; choosing TTL and watermark windows is a balance between correctness (late-arrivals) and bounded state size.
- Exactly-once semantics rely on Kafka + sink transactional guarantees; initial implementation will use at-least-once with dedupe layer to simplify rollout.
- Using BigQuery as canonical store increases write costs but gives auditability; alternative is ClickHouse for lower-cost high-throughput writes but with less natural cross-region replication.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototyping: local Kafka + Flink job that groups sample production traces and emits canonical deltas (2 weeks). 2) Infra: provision regional read-only topics + staging BigQuery dataset, create monitoring metrics (delta_count, dedupe_rate, late_arrival_pct). 3) Shadow run: ingest production traffic in shadow mode, compare outputs vs current ledger for discrepancy metrics (3 weeks). 4) Canary: enable authoritative writes for a single low-volume tenant and monitor for mismatches (1 week). 5) Rollout: gradual rollout by tenant buckets with automatic rollback thresholds.
metrics_to_track: settled_latency (time from first fragment to settled delta)
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for fragment compaction logic and deterministic canonical hashing.
- Property tests: reordering/replay simulation to ensure idempotency.
- End-to-end test harness replaying stored production fragments into a staging pipeline and asserting aggregate token counts equal baseline after reconciliation.
- Manual verification of audit columns for sample tenants (edge_id provenance, request_chain).
rollout_checks: Thresholds for automatic rollback: delta_discrepancy_rate > 0.5% for a rolling 3h window OR customer_charge_delta_95p > $1.00 for any tenant. Must have alerting runbook and pager coverage during canary window.
